plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. Since I win only if I have the highest bid, and I pay the second-highest bid (not my own), there's no incentive to shade my bid up or down. Bidding exactly my value of $19 ensures I win whenever it's profitable to do so (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction) where the highest bidder wins but pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of what others bid. If I underbid, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. If I overbid, I risk winning and paying more than my value. With a private value of $44, I should bid exactly $44 to ensure optimal outcomes.

This is a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), which is a Vickrey auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do - it maximizes expected profit. Bidding higher than value risks winning at a price exceeding value (loss), while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $43, I should bid exactly $43 to ensure optimal expected outcomes in this one-shot game.
